content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward spikes, leading to overcorrection in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model prematurely assumes prices will return to historical averages.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizons show persistent bias toward lower values, especially when recent history includes strong downward momentum.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility spikes in the final 5–7 days of the forecast window.
- When true prices rise sharply, model reacts slowly and underestimates the magnitude.
- Forecast tends to be overly conservative in the first 10 days, then gradually adjusts — but often too late to catch momentum.
